```{r sample_triage, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE, echo=TRUE}
                              sum(triage_df$n_axes > 1), " of ", nrow(triage_df),
                              " wells carry more than one axis."))
# Print to RMarkdown
knitr::kable(
  triage_df, 
  caption = "TRIAGED SAMPLES"
)

warn_samps$Triage <- warn_samps$`Sample Name` %in% triage_df$SampleID
knitr::kable(
  warn_samps %>% select(`Sample Name`, `IC Median`, Detectability, `QC Status`,Triage), 
  caption = "ALAMAR WARN SAMPLES"
)

#Flagged excessive_matching_reads (not removed)
read_outliers$Triage <- read_outliers$SampleID %in% triage_df$SampleID
knitr::kable(
  read_outliers %>% select(SampleID, Run, Bay, Reads, Triage), 
  caption = "FLAGGED SAMPLES"
)
  
# Save to CSV
write_csv(triage_df, "output_files/samples_to_triage.csv")

# Remove triaged samples from main dataset
combined_qc_filtered <- combined_qc %>%
  rownames_to_column("SampleID") %>%
  filter(!SampleID %in% triage_df$SampleID) %>%
  column_to_rownames("SampleID")

#Add count summary
qc_summary <- combined_qc_filtered %>%
  group_by(Run, Bay) %>%
  summarise(combined_qc_filtered = n(), .groups = "drop") %>%
  arrange(Run, Bay)

knitr::kable(
  qc_summary, 
  caption = "Summary of post-QC counts:"
)

```

## D.4 Per-plate QC Summary
One row per plate: post-QC retained count, our triaged and flagged samples, and Alamar warnings.

```{r per_plate_summary, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE, echo=TRUE}
plate_lookup <- alamar_qc %>%
  transmute(SampleID = `Sample Name`,
            Run = stringr::str_extract(plateID, "^[0-9]{8}-[0-9]{4}"),
            Bay = stringr::str_extract(plateID, "Bay[0-9]+"))

count_by_plate <- function(ids, nm) {
  tibble(SampleID = unique(as.character(ids))) %>%
    inner_join(plate_lookup, by = "SampleID") %>%
    count(Run, Bay, name = nm)
}

plate_summary <- plate_lookup %>%
  distinct(Run, Bay) %>%
  left_join(qc_summary %>% rename(Retained_postQC = combined_qc_filtered), by = c("Run","Bay")) %>%
  left_join(count_by_plate(triage_df$SampleID,       "Triaged"),         by = c("Run","Bay")) %>%
  left_join(count_by_plate(read_outliers$SampleID,   "Flagged_Reads"),   by = c("Run","Bay")) %>%
  left_join(count_by_plate(warn_samps$`Sample Name`, "Alamar_Warnings"), by = c("Run","Bay")) %>%
  mutate(across(c(Retained_postQC, Triaged, Flagged_Reads, Alamar_Warnings),
                ~ tidyr::replace_na(., 0L))) %>%
  arrange(Run, Bay)

knitr::kable(
  plate_summary,
  caption = "Per-plate QC summary: pipeline triage/flags vs. Alamar warnings"
) %>%
  kableExtra::kable_styling(full_width = TRUE,
                            bootstrap_options = c("striped", "hover", "condensed"))

write_csv(plate_summary, "output_files/per_plate_QC_summary.csv")
```

## D.5 QC Screen Audit

Everything above asks *what happened to the samples*. This section asks **whether
the screens are any good**: does each gate fire at all, is it independent of the
others, where does its cut sit on its own statistic, and is it keying on plate
position rather than on the specimen.

**Diagnostic only. Nothing here removes or flags a sample.**

```{r audit-setup, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE, echo=TRUE}
# The audit universe: every well that entered the screens.
audit <- tibble(SampleID = rownames(combined_qc),
                Run = combined_qc$Run, Bay = combined_qc$Bay) %>%
  mutate(plate = paste(Run, Bay)) %>%
  left_join(well_pos %>% select(SampleID, Well, wellRow, wellCol), by = "SampleID") %>%
  left_join(intensity_df %>% select(SampleID, mean_INT, mean_INT_z, intensity_flag),
            by = "SampleID") %>%
  left_join(matching_outliers %>% select(SampleID, Reads, High_Read_Plate, Low_Read),
            by = "SampleID") %>%
  left_join(df_temp %>% select(SampleID, IC_Reads, Median_Value, IC_Outlier = Outlier_Flag),
            by = "SampleID") %>%
  left_join(alamar_qc %>% transmute(SampleID = `Sample Name`,
                                    IC_Median = suppressWarnings(as.numeric(`IC Median`)) / .ic_scale,
                                    Detectability = suppressWarnings(as.numeric(Detectability)),
                                    QC_Status = `QC Status`),
            by = "SampleID") %>%
  left_join(triage_df %>% select(SampleID, Reason, tri_low_reads, tri_IC, tri_PCA, tri_burden,
                                 tri_bad_data, n_axes), by = "SampleID") %>%
  left_join(burden_stat %>% select(SampleID, fdr_min, n_out), by = "SampleID") %>%
  left_join(pca_df %>% select(SampleID = Sample, PC_z_round1 = PC_z,
                              PC_z_cohort, pca_cohort_flag, pca_masked_by_plate), by = "SampleID") %>%
  mutate(across(c(tri_low_reads, tri_IC, tri_PCA, tri_burden, tri_bad_data, High_Read_Plate, Low_Read,
                  IC_Outlier), ~ tidyr::replace_na(., FALSE)),
         triaged      = SampleID %in% triage_df$SampleID,
         read_flagged = SampleID %in% read_outliers$SampleID,
         n_axes       = tidyr::replace_na(n_axes, 0L))

# Detectability arrives as a 0-1 proportion or a 0-100 percent depending on the
# export; put it on 0-1 so the vendor bar below means one thing.
if (max(audit$Detectability, na.rm = TRUE) > 1.5) audit$Detectability <- audit$Detectability / 100

cat(sprintf("Audit universe: %d wells, %d plate-bays, %d distinct well positions.\n",
            nrow(audit), dplyr::n_distinct(audit$plate), dplyr::n_distinct(audit$Well)))
```

### D.5.1 Does each gate fire?

A gate that fires on **zero** wells has not been shown to be safe — it has not
been tested. It could be correctly finding nothing, or it could be unreachable by
construction. Those are very different, and the count alone cannot tell them
apart, so the headroom to each cut is reported next to it.

```{r gate-inventory, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE, echo=TRUE}
gate_row <- function(gate, action, fired, n, headroom = NA_character_, note = "") {
  tibble(gate, action, n_fired = sum(fired, na.rm = TRUE), n_eval = n,
         pct = round(100 * sum(fired, na.rm = TRUE) / n, 3),
         headroom, status = ifelse(sum(fired, na.rm = TRUE) == 0,
                                   "INERT - untested, not proven safe", "fires"),
         note)
}
N <- nrow(audit)
.hr <- function(x, cut) sprintf("max %.3f vs cut %.3f (%+.3f)", x, cut, x - cut)

gate_inventory <- bind_rows(
  gate_row("triage: IC outlier", "REMOVE", audit$tri_IC, N,
           sprintf("%d of %d plate-bays have the 1000 floor binding",
                   sum(ic_geom$floor_binds), nrow(ic_geom)),
           "same quantity as the vendor IC Median metric - see D.2.3"),
  gate_row("triage: PCA round 1", "REMOVE", audit$SampleID %in% extreme_samples_round1, N,
           .hr(max(pca_df$PC_z, na.rm = TRUE), PCA_SD), ""),
  gate_row("triage: PCA round 2", "REMOVE", audit$SampleID %in% extreme_samples_round2, N,
           if (nrow(pca_df2)) .hr(max(pca_df2$PC_z, na.rm = TRUE), PCA_SD) else "not run",
           "second pass, after round-1 outliers are removed"),
  gate_row("triage: outlier burden", "REMOVE", audit$tri_burden, N,
           local({
             below <- op_points$fdr_min[op_points$fdr_min <  FDR_threshold]
             above <- op_points$fdr_min[op_points$fdr_min >= FDR_threshold]
             if (!length(below) || !length(above)) "cut is outside the observed FDR range"
             else sprintf("cut sits between FDR %.4g and %.4g - nothing to tune between",
                          max(below), min(above))
           }),
           "quantised: an integer anchor count, not a dial"),
  gate_row("triage: bad data", "REMOVE", audit$tri_bad_data, N, NA_character_,
           "non-numeric NPQ entries"),
  gate_row("flag: high reads (plate-relative)", "FLAG", audit$High_Read_Plate, N,
           NA_character_, ""),
  gate_row("flag: low reads", "FLAG", audit$Low_Read, N,
           sprintf("plate-relative lower bound reachable in %d of %d bays",
                   sum(read_gate_geometry$lower_is_plate_relative), nrow(read_gate_geometry)),
           "absolute floor in practice - see D.2.4"),
  # Vendor bars come from the export's own preamble (section B), so this audit
  # stays correct if Alamar changes one, and uses the right bar for the matrix.
  gate_row(sprintf("vendor: Detectability < %.0f%%", 100 * vendor_thresholds$detectability_min),
           "vendor warning", audit$Detectability < vendor_thresholds$detectability_min, N,
           NA_character_,
           sprintf("Alamar QC Status driver; bar is for %s", vendor_thresholds$sample_matrix)),
  gate_row(sprintf("vendor: |IC Median| > %.2f", vendor_thresholds$ic_median),
           "vendor warning", abs(audit$IC_Median) > vendor_thresholds$ic_median, N,
           NA_character_, "Alamar QC Status driver"),
  gate_row(sprintf("vendor: IC Reads < %s", format(vendor_thresholds$ic_reads_min, big.mark = ",")),
           "vendor warning", audit$IC_Reads < vendor_thresholds$ic_reads_min, N,
           sprintf("lowest IC Reads seen: %s",
                   format(min(audit$IC_Reads, na.rm = TRUE), big.mark = ",")), ""),
  gate_row(sprintf("vendor: Reads < %s",
                   format(vendor_thresholds$reads_min, big.mark = ",", scientific = FALSE)),
           "vendor warning", audit$Reads < vendor_thresholds$reads_min, N,
           sprintf("lowest Reads seen: %s",
                   format(min(audit$Reads, na.rm = TRUE), big.mark = ",")), ""),
  gate_row("informational: whole-panel intensity", "NONE - reported only",
           audit$intensity_flag %in% c("HIGH", "LOW"), N,
           sprintf("range %.2f to %.2f SD", min(audit$mean_INT_z, na.rm = TRUE),
                   max(audit$mean_INT_z, na.rm = TRUE)),
           "D.0 - a covariate, never a gate")
)
write_csv(gate_inventory, "output_files/qc_gate_inventory.csv")

knitr::kable(gate_inventory, caption = "QC gate inventory: what each screen actually did") %>%
  kableExtra::kable_styling(full_width = TRUE,
                            bootstrap_options = c("striped", "hover", "condensed"))

.inert <- gate_inventory$gate[gate_inventory$n_fired == 0]
if (length(.inert))
  cat(sprintf("\nINERT on this run (%d): %s\n  These are UNTESTED. Check the headroom column before assuming they are simply finding nothing.\n",
              length(.inert), paste(.inert, collapse = "; ")))
```

### D.5.2 Are the gates independent of each other?

If two screens remove the same wells they are one screen reported twice, and the
methods text should not present them as corroborating each other.

```{r gate-overlap, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE, echo=TRUE}
axes <- c(tri_IC = "IC", tri_PCA = "PCA", tri_burden = "burden")
pairs <- utils::combn(names(axes), 2, simplify = FALSE)
gate_overlap <- bind_rows(lapply(pairs, function(p) {
  a <- audit[[p[1]]]; b <- audit[[p[2]]]
  tibble(gate_a = axes[[p[1]]], gate_b = axes[[p[2]]],
         n_a = sum(a), n_b = sum(b), n_both = sum(a & b),
         jaccard = round(sum(a & b) / max(1, sum(a | b)), 3))
}))
# The read flag is a flag, not a triage axis, but "is it just triage again?" is
# the same question.
gate_overlap <- bind_rows(gate_overlap, tibble(
  gate_a = "read flag", gate_b = "any triage",
  n_a = sum(audit$read_flagged), n_b = sum(audit$triaged),
  n_both = sum(audit$read_flagged & audit$triaged),
  jaccard = round(sum(audit$read_flagged & audit$triaged) /
                    max(1, sum(audit$read_flagged | audit$triaged)), 3)))
write_csv(gate_overlap, "output_files/qc_gate_overlap.csv")
knitr::kable(gate_overlap, caption = "Pairwise overlap between screens (Jaccard)")
```

### D.5.3 Where does each cut sit on its own statistic?

The nearest retained well and the nearest removed well on each axis. If they are
touching, the cut is splitting a continuum rather than separating two
populations, and the exact threshold is doing more work than it looks.

```{r cut-neighbourhood, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE, echo=TRUE}
cut_nbhd <- function(stat, removed, gate, cut) {
  ok <- !is.na(stat)
  if (!any(ok & removed) || !any(ok & !removed)) return(NULL)
  # Statistics here are all "larger = worse" except IC Median, handled by caller.
  tibble(gate, cut,
         nearest_removed = round(min(stat[ok & removed]), 4),
         nearest_retained = round(max(stat[ok & !removed]), 4),
         gap = round(min(stat[ok & removed]) - max(stat[ok & !removed]), 4))
}
# FDR can be exactly 0, so clamp before the log rather than carrying an Inf into
# the min/max below.
.nlp <- -log10(pmax(audit$fdr_min, .Machine$double.xmin))
# Our IC gate fires on |IC Reads / plate median - 1| > 0.40, so that ratio — not
# the vendor's IC Median — is the statistic its own cut sits on.
.ic_stat <- abs(audit$IC_Reads / audit$Median_Value - 1)
gate_cuts <- bind_rows(
  cut_nbhd(.ic_stat, audit$tri_IC, "IC (|IC reads / plate median - 1|)", 0.40),
  cut_nbhd(audit$PC_z_round1, audit$SampleID %in% extreme_samples_round1,
           "PCA round 1 (PC_z)", PCA_SD),
  cut_nbhd(.nlp, audit$tri_burden, "burden (-log10 FDR)", round(-log10(FDR_threshold), 4)),
  # Cross-axis, and labelled as such: how far our call sits from the vendor bar.
  # A negative gap here is disagreement between two gates, not a split population.
  cut_nbhd(abs(audit$IC_Median), audit$tri_IC,
           "our IC call read against the VENDOR statistic", ic_median_thresh)
)
write_csv(gate_cuts, "output_files/gate_cut_neighbourhood.csv")
knitr::kable(gate_cuts, caption = "Nearest removed vs nearest retained well on each axis. A gap at or below 0 means the cut lands inside a continuous population.")
```

### D.5.4 Is a screen keying on plate position rather than on the specimen?

A well position that is triaged far more often than the others across many plates
is a **layout or hardware** problem, not a specimen problem — and it is invisible
to every within-plate screen above, because each of those only ever compares a
well to its own plate.

The test is a permutation, not a chi-square: triage counts spread over ~96
positions leave most cells at 0 or 1, where an asymptotic test is not conservative
but wrong. Labels are shuffled **within each plate-bay**, holding each plate's
triage count fixed, so plate-level effects cannot manufacture a position signal.
The statistic is the **maximum** per-position count, which needs no further
multiple-testing correction.

> **On the word "site".** This asks about the *physical site on the plate*.
> Clustering by **clinical collection site** is a different and equally important
> question, and it cannot be asked here: Primary QC is deliberately agnostic to
> phenotype and covariates, and the site label only exists after the metadata
> merge. The well-level table in D.5.6 carries every gate flag keyed by
> `SampleID` precisely so that question can be answered downstream with a single
> join — see `Secondary_QC/Triage_Review/`.

```{r position-effects, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE, echo=TRUE}
set.seed(123)

perm_max_position <- function(flag, pos, plate, n_perm) {
  keep <- !is.na(pos) & !is.na(flag)
  flag <- flag[keep]; pos <- pos[keep]; plate <- plate[keep]
  lev  <- sort(unique(pos))
  obs_counts <- tabulate(match(pos[flag], lev), nbins = length(lev))
  obs <- max(obs_counts)
  # Under the null, each plate's k flagged wells are a uniform random subset of
  # that plate's wells. Draw per plate, so plate composition is held fixed.
  pos_by_plate <- split(pos, plate)
  k_by_plate   <- vapply(split(flag, plate), sum, integer(1))
  null <- replicate(n_perm, {
    drawn <- unlist(Map(function(pp, k) if (k > 0) sample(pp, k) else pp[0],
                        pos_by_plate, k_by_plate), use.names = FALSE)
    max(tabulate(match(drawn, lev), nbins = length(lev)))
  })
  list(obs = obs, p = (1 + sum(null >= obs)) / (n_perm + 1),
       null_mean = mean(null),
       tab = tibble(Well = lev, n_flagged = obs_counts,
                    n_wells = as.integer(table(factor(pos, levels = lev)))) %>%
             mutate(pct = round(100 * n_flagged / n_wells, 2)) %>%
             arrange(desc(n_flagged)))
}

if (all(is.na(audit$Well))) {
  cat("No well positions available — plate-position diagnostics skipped.\n")
} else {
  pe_tri  <- perm_max_position(audit$triaged,      audit$Well, audit$plate, n_perm)
  pe_read <- perm_max_position(audit$read_flagged, audit$Well, audit$plate, n_perm)

  write_csv(pe_tri$tab,  "output_files/well_position_effects.csv")
  write_csv(pe_read$tab, "output_files/well_position_effects_readflag.csv")

  cat(sprintf("Triage by position: worst well is %s at %d of %d (%.1f%%), against %.1f%% elsewhere.\n",
              pe_tri$tab$Well[1], pe_tri$tab$n_flagged[1], pe_tri$tab$n_wells[1],
              pe_tri$tab$pct[1],
              100 * sum(pe_tri$tab$n_flagged[-1]) / sum(pe_tri$tab$n_wells[-1])))
  cat(sprintf("  permutation on the maximum: observed %d, null mean %.2f, p = %.4f\n",
              pe_tri$obs, pe_tri$null_mean, pe_tri$p))
  cat(sprintf("Read flags by position: max %d, null mean %.2f, p = %.4f\n",
              pe_read$obs, pe_read$null_mean, pe_read$p))

  knitr::kable(head(pe_tri$tab, 10),
               caption = "Most-triaged well positions across all plate-bays")

  # Which axis does the worst position exit on? A single axis points at one
  # mechanism; a spread points at a generally bad well.
  .w <- pe_tri$tab$Well[1]
  .wa <- audit %>% filter(Well == .w, triaged) %>%
    summarise(IC = sum(tri_IC), PCA = sum(tri_PCA), burden = sum(tri_burden),
              bad_data = sum(tri_bad_data))
  cat(sprintf("Position %s exits via: IC %d, PCA %d, burden %d, bad data %d\n",
              .w, .wa$IC, .wa$PCA, .wa$burden, .wa$bad_data))
}
```

#### Is there a standing spatial gradient underneath it?

A single bad position is usually the extreme of a smooth trend across the plate
rather than an isolated defect. The IC is the right quantity to look at: NPQ is
normalised to it, so a position that recovers less IC shifts every reported value
for the specimen that lands there.

```{r position-gradient, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE, echo=TRUE}
if (!all(is.na(audit$Well))) {
  pos_map <- audit %>%
    filter(!is.na(Well), !is.na(IC_Median)) %>%
    group_by(Well, wellRow, wellCol) %>%
    summarise(n = n(), median_IC_Median = round(median(IC_Median, na.rm = TRUE), 4),
              median_mean_INT = round(median(mean_INT, na.rm = TRUE), 4), .groups = "drop") %>%
    arrange(median_IC_Median)
  write_csv(pos_map, "output_files/position_map_IC.csv")

  print(
    ggplot(pos_map, aes(x = factor(wellCol), y = factor(wellRow, levels = rev(sort(unique(wellRow)))),
                        fill = median_IC_Median)) +
      geom_tile(colour = "white") +
      scale_fill_gradient2(low = "#B2182B", mid = "#F7F7F7", high = "#2166AC", midpoint = 0) +
      theme_minimal() +
      labs(title = "Median IC recovery by plate position, pooled over all plate-bays",
           subtitle = "Red = this position systematically recovers less IC than its plate",
           x = "Column", y = "Row", fill = "median\nIC Median")
  )

  # Pre-specified direction: does IC recovery fall from row A to row H? Reported
  # per plate-bay, so a single odd plate cannot carry it.
  row_grad <- audit %>%
    filter(!is.na(wellRow), !is.na(IC_Median)) %>%
    mutate(row_i = match(wellRow, LETTERS)) %>%
    group_by(Run, Bay) %>%
    filter(dplyr::n_distinct(row_i) > 2) %>%
    summarise(spearman = suppressWarnings(cor(row_i, IC_Median, method = "spearman",
                                              use = "complete.obs")),
              .groups = "drop")
  write_csv(row_grad, "output_files/ic_row_gradient.csv")
  cat(sprintf("IC recovery falls from row A to row H in %d of %d plate-bays (median rho %.2f).\n",
              sum(row_grad$spearman < 0, na.rm = TRUE), nrow(row_grad),
              median(row_grad$spearman, na.rm = TRUE)))

  # --- region contrasts, permuted within plate ------------------------------
  # One helper, used for every region test below. Shuffling the region label
  # WITHIN each plate-bay means a plate that simply ran low overall cannot
  # manufacture a contrast.
  cor_df <- audit %>% filter(!is.na(Well), !is.na(IC_Median))
  region_test <- function(inreg, label) {
    inreg <- !is.na(inreg) & inreg
    if (!any(inreg) || !any(!inreg)) return(invisible(NULL))
    obs <- median(cor_df$IC_Median[inreg], na.rm = TRUE) -
           median(cor_df$IC_Median[!inreg], na.rm = TRUE)
    ord <- order(paste(cor_df$Run, cor_df$Bay))
    v   <- cor_df$IC_Median[ord]
    grp <- split(seq_along(ord), paste(cor_df$Run, cor_df$Bay)[ord])
    lab <- inreg[ord]
    nul <- replicate(n_perm, {
      s <- logical(length(lab)); for (g in grp) s[g] <- sample(lab[g])
      median(v[s], na.rm = TRUE) - median(v[!s], na.rm = TRUE)
    })
    cat(sprintf("  %-34s %+.4f vs %+.4f elsewhere  diff %+.4f  perm p = %.4f\n",
                label, median(cor_df$IC_Median[inreg], na.rm = TRUE),
                median(cor_df$IC_Median[!inreg], na.rm = TRUE), obs,
                (1 + sum(abs(nul) >= abs(obs))) / (n_perm + 1)))
    invisible(obs)
  }

  # Layout-agnostic and always run: no region is named in advance, so these are
  # valid on any plate geometry and cannot be accused of picking their target.
  cat("Spatial structure (permuted within plate-bay):\n")
  .rl <- sort(unique(cor_df$wellRow)); .cl <- sort(unique(cor_df$wellCol))
  if (length(.rl) > 2 && length(.cl) > 2)
    region_test(cor_df$wellRow %in% .rl[c(1, length(.rl))] |
                cor_df$wellCol %in% .cl[c(1, length(.cl))], "edge vs interior")

  # Column gradient, the companion to the row gradient above.
  col_grad <- audit %>%
    filter(!is.na(wellCol), !is.na(IC_Median)) %>%
    group_by(Run, Bay) %>%
    filter(dplyr::n_distinct(wellCol) > 2) %>%
    summarise(spearman = suppressWarnings(cor(wellCol, IC_Median, method = "spearman",
                                              use = "complete.obs")), .groups = "drop")
  cat(sprintf("  IC recovery falls left-to-right in %d of %d plate-bays (median rho %.2f)\n",
              sum(col_grad$spearman < 0, na.rm = TRUE), nrow(col_grad),
              median(col_grad$spearman, na.rm = TRUE)))

  # The empirically worst quadrant, reported DESCRIPTIVELY. No p-value: the
  # region was chosen by looking, so any p-value here would be a search result
  # dressed as a test. It is a lead for the next run's `prior_region`.
  .rq <- .rl[seq_len(ceiling(length(.rl) / 2))]; .cq <- .cl[seq_len(ceiling(length(.cl) / 2))]
  quads <- list("top-left" = list(.rq, .cq),
                "top-right" = list(.rq, setdiff(.cl, .cq)),
                "bottom-left" = list(setdiff(.rl, .rq), .cq),
                "bottom-right" = list(setdiff(.rl, .rq), setdiff(.cl, .cq)))
  qd <- vapply(quads, function(q) {
    i <- cor_df$wellRow %in% q[[1]] & cor_df$wellCol %in% q[[2]]
    if (!any(i)) NA_real_ else median(cor_df$IC_Median[i], na.rm = TRUE) -
      median(cor_df$IC_Median[!i], na.rm = TRUE) }, numeric(1))
  cat(sprintf("  lowest-IC quadrant (descriptive, chosen by looking): %s at %+.4f vs rest\n",
              names(qd)[which.min(qd)], min(qd, na.rm = TRUE)))
  cat("    -> to TEST it, set prior_region in A.3 and re-run on the NEXT dataset.\n")

  # Confirmatory only if a region was named in advance (A.3 `prior_region`).
  if (!is.null(prior_region)) {
    pr <- cor_df$wellRow %in% prior_region$rows & cor_df$wellCol %in% prior_region$cols
    cat("Prior-specified region (named before this run, so this p-value is confirmatory):\n")
    region_test(pr, sprintf("rows %s x cols %s",
                            paste(prior_region$rows, collapse = ""),
                            paste(range(prior_region$cols), collapse = "-")))
  }
}
```

### D.5.5 The intensity axis against the gates

`mean_INT` (D.0) is the level statistic none of the gates compute. Reading each
triage class against it shows what each screen is actually selecting — and
whether the pipeline is quietly reshaping the intensity distribution.

**Report per class, never pooled.** The classes point in opposite directions on
this axis, so a pooled mean describes none of them.

```{r intensity-vs-gates, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE, echo=TRUE}
cohens_d <- function(x, y) {
  x <- x[!is.na(x)]; y <- y[!is.na(y)]
  if (length(x) < 2 || length(y) < 2) return(NA_real_)
  s <- sqrt(((length(x)-1)*var(x) + (length(y)-1)*var(y)) / (length(x)+length(y)-2))
  if (!is.finite(s) || s == 0) return(NA_real_)
  (mean(x) - mean(y)) / s
}
auc <- function(x, y) {   # P(random x > random y), ties at 0.5
  x <- x[!is.na(x)]; y <- y[!is.na(y)]
  if (!length(x) || !length(y)) return(NA_real_)
  r <- rank(c(x, y))
  (sum(r[seq_along(x)]) - length(x) * (length(x) + 1) / 2) / (length(x) * length(y))
}

ref <- audit$mean_INT_z[!audit$triaged & !audit$read_flagged]
classes <- list(
  "triaged (ALL - do not read this row)" = audit$triaged,
  "  IC only"        = audit$tri_IC & audit$n_axes == 1,
  "  PCA (any axis)" = audit$tri_PCA,
  "  burden (any axis)" = audit$tri_burden,
  "read-flagged HIGH" = audit$read_flagged & audit$High_Read_Plate
)
axis_attr <- bind_rows(lapply(names(classes), function(nm) {
  v <- audit$mean_INT_z[classes[[nm]]]
  tibble(class = nm, n = sum(classes[[nm]], na.rm = TRUE),
         mean_INT_z = round(mean(v, na.rm = TRUE), 3),
         cohens_d = round(cohens_d(v, ref), 3),
         AUC = round(auc(v, ref), 3))
}))
write_csv(axis_attr, "output_files/qc_axis_attribution.csv")
knitr::kable(axis_attr,
             caption = "Each triage class on the whole-panel intensity axis, against retained wells")

# Does QC reshape the intensity distribution, or only clip its tail? The moment
# skewness will move simply from deleting extreme points; a robust measure will
# not, unless the body of the distribution really changed.
bowley <- function(v) { q <- stats::quantile(v, c(.25,.5,.75), na.rm = TRUE)
  unname((q[3] + q[1] - 2*q[2]) / (q[3] - q[1])) }
m3 <- function(v) { v <- v[!is.na(v)]; mean((v - mean(v))^3) / stats::sd(v)^3 }
pre  <- audit$mean_INT_z
post <- audit$mean_INT_z[!audit$triaged]
cat(sprintf("Intensity distribution, pre-triage -> post-triage:\n  moment skew %+.3f -> %+.3f    Bowley skew %+.3f -> %+.3f    range [%.2f, %.2f] -> [%.2f, %.2f]\n",
            m3(pre), m3(post), bowley(pre), bowley(post),
            min(pre, na.rm = TRUE), max(pre, na.rm = TRUE),
            min(post, na.rm = TRUE), max(post, na.rm = TRUE)))
cat("  If Bowley barely moves while the moment skew does, QC clipped a tail and did not reshape the body.\n")
cat("  Either way the intensity axis survives QC and still belongs in the analysis model.\n")
```

#### What to do with the read-flagged wells

They are **kept**, and that is the right call — but "the flag is redundant once
you model depth" is a stronger claim than this pipeline can support, and it
should not be written into methods text as though it had been established.

Two things to carry downstream:

* **Model `log2(Reads)`, per marker.** NPQ is IC-normalised and total reads are
  close to independent of IC reads, so a pure sequencing-depth effect ought to
  divide out and leave slope 0. It does not — the depth slopes are strongly
  marker-specific, so one shared depth covariate will not absorb it identically
  across the panel.
* **"High-read" is a property of the well's neighbours.** The bound is
  plate-relative, so the same specimen run on a different plate need not be
  flagged. Treat the flag as a statement about a well, not about a subject.

### D.5.6 Well-level QC table

One row per well, carrying every gate flag, the intensity axis, plate position
and read/IC statistics. This is the join key for anything downstream that needs
to ask a question Primary QC cannot — above all **clustering by clinical
collection site**, which needs the metadata merge.

```{r well-level-table, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE, echo=TRUE}
well_qc <- audit %>%
  transmute(SampleID, Run, Bay, Well, wellRow, wellCol,
            triaged, Reason, n_axes, tri_low_reads, tri_IC, tri_PCA, tri_burden, tri_bad_data,
            read_flagged, High_Read_Plate, Low_Read,
            mean_INT, mean_INT_z, intensity_flag,
            Reads, IC_Reads, IC_ratio_to_plate_median = round(IC_Reads / Median_Value, 4),
            IC_Median, Detectability, QC_Status,
            PC_z_round1 = round(PC_z_round1, 3),
            PC_z_cohort = round(PC_z_cohort, 3), pca_cohort_flag, pca_masked_by_plate,
            burden_fdr_min = fdr_min,
            burden_n_out = n_out) %>%
  arrange(Run, Bay, Well)

write_csv(well_qc, "output_files/well_level_QC.csv")
cat(sprintf("Wrote output_files/well_level_QC.csv: %d wells x %d columns\n",
            nrow(well_qc), ncol(well_qc)))
knitr::kable(head(well_qc %>% select(SampleID, Run, Bay, Well, triaged, n_axes,
                                     read_flagged, mean_INT_z, Reads), 10),
             caption = "well_level_QC.csv (first 10 rows, subset of columns)")
```

# E. Biomarker QC
Reintegrate biomarkers and separate into groups.

## E.1 Re-integrate High-Corr Biomarkers 
Here we add back in high-correlation biomarkers that were removed for the QC Biomarker Set. These all should have good detectability and raw read counts.

```{r add_high_cor, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE, echo=TRUE}
# Add back high-correlated biomarkers to combined_qc_filtered
library(tibble)

# Rebuild the post-QC biomarker set EXPLICITLY as `qc_pool` (changed 2026-09-01).
#
# This used to cbind `high_cor` onto whatever columns combined_qc_filtered happened to carry, which
# was correct only while the anchors were guaranteed to be a subset of qc_pool. Since the WATCH-tier
# fix an anchor may sit BELOW the 98% pool bar (kept for triage, flagged), and cbind would then
# promote it out of the Low file and into the standard post-QC set — silently changing biomarker
# CONTENT, which the frozen/rederive design guarantees is mode-invariant.
#
# Stating the content set directly removes that coupling: which markers reach the post-QC datasets is
# `qc_pool` and nothing else, no matter what anchored the triage. Identical to the old result whenever
# anchors are a subset of qc_pool, which is every pre-2026-09-01 run.
combined_qc_full <- combined_df[rownames(combined_qc_filtered),
                                c("Run", "Bay", qc_pool), drop = FALSE]
stopifnot(setequal(setdiff(colnames(combined_qc_full), c("Run", "Bay")), qc_pool))
# Move SampleIDs to first column
combined_qc_full <- rownames_to_column(combined_qc_full, var = "SampleID")

knitr::kable(
  high_cor, 
  caption = "High-correlation biomarkers added back:"
)
dim(combined_qc_full)[2]-3 #NUMBER OF BIOMARKERS IS COLUMNS-3
```

## E.2 Low-detectability Biomarkers

### E.2.1 Re-integrate Det>50% Biomarkers 
Alamar suggests that the detectability threshold should be 50%. Here we add back in Biomarkers with minimum detectability>50% that were dropped to create the QC Biomarker set. We also require these to have raw read counts above the threshold. Those with low counts are further examined in later QC steps.

```{r add_med_det, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE, echo=TRUE}
# Add back biomarkers with >50% Min_Detectability ("medium detectability")
med_det <- low_det[low_det$Min_Detectability > min_detectability, ]

# Split into "good" and "still low count"
good_detect <- med_det[!(med_det$Biomarker %in% low_counts$Biomarker), ]
med_det_low_counts <- med_det[(med_det$Biomarker %in% low_counts$Biomarker), ]

# Extract good biomarker names
good_detect_names <- good_detect$Biomarker

# Subset combined_df to keep only good samples and these biomarkers
med_det_subset <- combined_df[rownames(combined_qc_filtered), good_detect_names, drop = FALSE]

# Add these columns back to the filtered QC dataset
combined_qc_full <- cbind(combined_qc_full, med_det_subset)
rownames(combined_qc_full) <- NULL

# Confirm dimensions
dim(combined_qc_full)[2]-3 #NUMBER OF BIOMARKERS IS COLUMNS-3

# Detectability metadata tables for each group
med_detect_table <- detect[detect$Biomarker %in% good_detect_names, ]
med_det_low_counts_table <- detect[detect$Biomarker %in% med_det_low_counts$Biomarker, ]

# View tables
knitr::kable(
  med_detect_table, 
  caption = "Medium-detectability (min det>50%) biomarkers added back:"
)
knitr::kable(
  med_det_low_counts_table, 
  caption = "Medium-detectability biomarkers with low counts to be examined below:"
)

```

### E.2.2 Re-examine Det<50% Biomarkers 
Look at these for possible re-integration, e.g., those with some expected low detectability.

```{r check_low_det, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE, echo=TRUE}
# Check biomarkers with <50% Min_Detectability to see if any should be added back in
library(kableExtra)

low_low_det <- low_det[low_det$Min_Detectability <= min_detectability, ]

# Split into "low detctability" and "low detectabiloty with low count"
low_detect <- low_low_det[!(low_low_det$Biomarker %in% low_counts$Biomarker), ]
low_det_low_counts <- low_low_det[(low_low_det$Biomarker %in% low_counts$Biomarker), ]

# Extract good biomarker names
low_detect_names <- low_detect$Biomarker

# Detectability metadata tables for each group
low_detect_table <- detect[detect$Biomarker %in% low_detect_names, ]
low_det_low_counts_table <- detect[detect$Biomarker %in% low_det_low_counts$Biomarker, ]

# View tables
knitr::kable(
  low_detect_table,
  caption = "Low-detectability (min det ≤50%) biomarkers with adequate read counts (routed to the Low output file):"
)
knitr::kable(
  low_det_low_counts_table, 
  caption = "Low-detectability biomarkers with low counts to be examined below:"
)

# Look for bimodal distributions and extreme outliers. Note differences across plates. Also LOD for these. 

#Pull LODs
# Read annotation data
annot <- read_csv("input_files/Annotation_Targets.csv")

# Select required columns
annot_sel <- annot %>%
  select(targetName, targetDetectability, targetLOD, targetLOD_NPQ, plateID)

 # Extract Run and Bay from plateID (assuming "YYYYMMDD_BayX" or similar format)
#CHANGED THIS FOR ALZ2 TO Allow for Runs with same prefix but different plates
annot_sel <- annot_sel %>%
  mutate(Run = str_extract(plateID, "\\d{8}-\\d+"),
         Bay = str_extract(plateID, "Bay\\d+"),
         RunBay = paste0(Run, "_", Bay))

# Make wide format table: LOD per Run/Bay
lod_matrix <- annot_sel %>%
  select(targetName, RunBay, targetLOD_NPQ) %>%
  distinct() %>%   # remove any duplicates
  pivot_wider(names_from = RunBay,
              values_from = targetLOD_NPQ)

# LOD for Reads
lod_reads_matrix <- annot_sel %>%
  select(targetName, RunBay, targetLOD) %>%
  distinct() %>%   # remove any duplicates
  pivot_wider(names_from = RunBay,
              values_from = targetLOD)

# Extract non-targetName columns
cols <- colnames(lod_matrix)[-1]

# Extract run date + bay index as ordering helpers
run_date <- str_extract(cols, "\\d{8}")
bay_num <- str_extract(cols, "(?<=Bay)\\d+") |> as.numeric()

# Create order index based on date then Bay number
col_order <- order(run_date, bay_num)

# Apply reordering: keep targetName first
lod_matrix <- lod_matrix %>%
  select(targetName, all_of(cols[col_order]))

# Reorder lod_reads_matrix columns to exactly match lod_matrix
lod_reads_matrix <- lod_reads_matrix %>%
  select(all_of(colnames(lod_matrix)))

write.csv(lod_matrix,"output_files/lod_matrix.csv", row.names = TRUE)
write.csv(lod_reads_matrix,"output_files/lod_reads_matrix.csv", row.names = TRUE)

cat("Plots of Low-detectability (min det<50%) biomarkers with good read counts:\n")
# Keep only rows in combined_qc_filtered and select relevant columns
combined_low_det <- combined_df %>%
  filter(rownames(.) %in% rownames(combined_qc_filtered)) %>%
  rownames_to_column("SampleID") %>%
  select(
    SampleID,
    Run,
    Bay,
    all_of(low_detect_names)
  )

# Ensure Run and Bay are factors
combined_low_det$Run <- factor(combined_low_det$Run)
combined_low_det$Bay <- factor(combined_low_det$Bay)

# Custom Bay colors
bay_colors <- c("Bay1" = "red", "Bay2" = "green", "Bay3" = "blue")

# Identify only biomarker columns
biomarker_cols <- setdiff(names(combined_low_det), c("SampleID", "Run", "Bay"))

# Loop and create violin plots for each biomarker
for (biom in biomarker_cols) {
  
  df_temp <- combined_low_det %>%
    select(Value = all_of(biom), Run, Bay)
  
  p <- ggplot(df_temp, aes(x = Run, y = Value, fill = Bay)) +
    geom_violin(alpha = 0.5, trim = FALSE, position = position_dodge(width = 0.8)) +
    geom_jitter(aes(color = Bay), 
                position = position_jitterdodge(jitter.width = 0.15, dodge.width = 0.8),
                alpha = 0.75, size = 1.3) +
    scale_fill_manual(values = bay_colors) +
    scale_color_manual(values = bay_colors) +
    theme_minimal() +
    labs(
      title = paste("Run × Bay Effects:", biom),
      x = "Run",
      y = biom
    ) +
    theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1))
  
  print(p)

 # ----- Print per-biomarker LOD table -----
lod_npq_vals <- lod_matrix[lod_matrix$targetName == biom, -1, drop = FALSE]
lod_read_vals <- lod_reads_matrix[lod_reads_matrix$targetName == biom, -1, drop = FALSE]

lod_table <- rbind(
  "NPQ LOD" = lod_npq_vals,
  "Read LOD" = lod_read_vals
)

# Print LOD table
print(cbind(rownames(lod_table),lod_table)) # I tried to make this prettier but it doesn't work in a loop
}

```


## E.3 Low Raw-Count Biomarkers  
Look at these more closely in secondary QC. Many are expected, because the protein is rare or they are due to a polymorphism, e.g., APOE4, BD-MAPT.

I'm showing NPQ values here for consistency, not raw read counts. Read counts will be examined further in secondary QC.
```{r check_low_raw_counts, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE, echo=TRUE}
# Examine low-count biomarkers 

# Vector of low-count biomarker names
low_counts_vec <- low_counts[[1]]  # assuming low_counts is a data frame with one column

# Keep only rows in combined_qc_filtered and select relevant columns
combined_low_counts <- combined_df %>%
  filter(rownames(.) %in% rownames(combined_qc_filtered)) %>%
  rownames_to_column("SampleID") %>%
  select(
    SampleID,
    Run,
    Bay,
    all_of(low_counts_vec)
  )

# Ensure Run and Bay are factors
combined_low_counts$Run <- factor(combined_low_counts$Run)
combined_low_counts$Bay <- factor(combined_low_counts$Bay)

# Custom Bay colors
bay_colors <- c("Bay1" = "red", "Bay2" = "green", "Bay3" = "blue")

# Identify only biomarker columns
biomarker_cols <- setdiff(names(combined_low_counts), c("SampleID", "Run", "Bay"))

# Loop and create violin plots for each biomarker
for (biom in biomarker_cols) {
  
  df_temp <- combined_low_counts %>%
    select(Value = all_of(biom), Run, Bay)
  
  p <- ggplot(df_temp, aes(x = Run, y = Value, fill = Bay)) +
     geom_violin(alpha = 0.5, trim = FALSE, position = position_dodge(width = 0.8)) +
     geom_jitter(aes(color = Bay), 
                position = position_jitterdodge(jitter.width = 0.15, dodge.width = 0.8),
                alpha = 0.75, size = 1.5) +
    scale_fill_manual(values = bay_colors) +
    scale_color_manual(values = bay_colors) +
    theme_minimal() +
    labs(
      title = paste("Run × Bay Effects:", biom),
      x = "Run",
      y = biom
    ) +
    theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1))
  
  print(p)
  # Print the row from combined_low_counts corresponding to this biomarker
  print(knitr::kable(low_counts[low_counts$Biomarker == biom, , drop = FALSE],caption = "Reads"))
}

```

# F. Prepare Output  
Output the QC'd dataset with samples from "Sample QC" removed. All biomarkers are included, but separated into two files: 1) NPQxxx_post_QC.csv and 2) NPQxxx_Low_post_QC.csv. 

1) Contains all biomarkers with minimum detectability >50% across plates for QC'd samples that have mean and median raw-read counts>500 across all plates.

2) Contains all biomarkers with minimum detectability <= 50% across plates and/or mean or median raw-read counts <= 500 across all plates or QC'd samples.

3) Contains all biomarkers in 1 for triaged samples.

4) Contains all biomarkers in 2 for triaged samples. 

Low detectability and low count biomarkers are in a separate dataset for "analysis". They are not necessarily bad, but will need to be analyzed differently from continuous biomarkers.

```{r make_output, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE, echo=TRUE}
# Here we save the QC'd files
# We may want to transpose them to be like original NPQ
library(dplyr)
library(tibble)

knitr::kable(
  summarize_counts(combined_qc_full, "QC'd Samples"), 
  caption = "POST-QC SAMPLES"
)

#Output file 1

cat("QC'd Biomarkers:", dim(combined_qc_full)[2]-3, "\n")
qc_file <- file.path("output_files", sub("\\.csv$", "_post_QC.csv", NPQ_data))
write.csv(combined_qc_full, qc_file, row.names = FALSE)  # SampleID is already a column; avoid a stray index col (matches files 2-4)
cat("Saved:", qc_file, "\n")

#Output file 2

# Remove duplicated metadata columns from the second dataset
combined_low_counts_nometadata <- combined_low_counts %>%
  select(-Run, -Bay)
# Perform the join on SampleID
combined_qc_low <- combined_low_det %>%
  left_join(combined_low_counts_nometadata, by = "SampleID")

cat("QC'd Low-count/Low-detectability Biomarkers:", dim(combined_qc_low)[2]-3, "\n")
qc_file <- file.path("output_files", sub("\\.csv$", "_Low_post_QC.csv", NPQ_data))
write.csv(combined_qc_low, qc_file, row.names = FALSE)
cat("Saved:", qc_file, "\n")

# Output file 3: TRIAGE × Full QC biomarkers

# sample list
triage_samples <- triage_df$SampleID
combined_df <- rownames_to_column(combined_df, "SampleID")

triage_qc_full <- combined_df %>%
  filter(SampleID %in% triage_samples) %>%
  select(any_of(colnames(combined_qc_full)))

triage_full_file <- file.path(
  "output_files", 
  sub("\\.csv$", "_post_QC_triage.csv", NPQ_data)
)

write.csv(triage_qc_full, triage_full_file, row.names = FALSE)
cat("Saved TRIAGE full-QC biomarker file:", triage_full_file, "\n")

# Output file 4: TRIAGE × Low QC biomarkers

triage_qc_low <- combined_df %>%
  filter(SampleID %in% triage_samples)%>%
  select(any_of(colnames(combined_qc_low)))

triage_low_file <- file.path(
  "output_files", 
  sub("\\.csv$", "_Low_post_QC_triage.csv", NPQ_data)
)

write.csv(triage_qc_low, triage_low_file, row.names = FALSE)
cat("Saved TRIAGE low-QC biomarker file:", triage_low_file, "\n")

```

# G.  Notes

## G.1 What the 2026-07-30 audit revision changed, and what it deliberately did not

Implements `Secondary_QC/Triage_Review/README.md`. **No sample's fate changed.**
Triage and flag membership are identical to the previous version; what changed is
what the pipeline measures and says about itself.

**Added**

* **D.0 `mean_INT`** — whole-panel intensity, computed pre-triage over all wells
  so removed wells are on the same scale as retained ones. Reported, never gated.
* **D.5** — the screen audit: gate inventory with INERT detection and headroom,
  gate overlap, cut neighbourhoods, plate-position permutation tests, the
  intensity axis read against each triage class, and `well_level_QC.csv`.
* **Per-axis triage booleans** (`tri_IC`, `tri_PCA`, `tri_burden`,
  `tri_bad_data`, `n_axes`) on `samples_to_triage.csv`.
* **`PC_z`** on both PCA coordinate files, so the operating point is auditable.

**Corrected in the reporting, not in the arithmetic**

* The **read gate is one-sided in practice.** Its lower bound is not
  plate-relative on any real run and cannot be made so — see D.2.4, where four
  alternative fences are shown to fail. The gate is now described and reported as
  a plate-relative *high* flag plus an absolute floor. The `pmax()` is retained,
  so behaviour is unchanged and the plate-relative bound will bind if a run ever
  supports it.
* **Our IC gate is Alamar's `IC Median` recomputed**, not an independent
  in-house check (Jaccard 0.966 on the 50-plate run). Methods text should not
  present it as a second opinion. It supplies roughly three quarters of triage.
* **`FDR_threshold` is not a dial.** It is an integer count of anchors wearing a
  p-value. D.2.2 prints the complete list of settings that exist.
* **`exit_reason`-style one-reason-per-well reports are not axis totals.**
  Precedence gives a valid partition, but it undercut the PCA axis by 37.5% and
  the burden axis by 64% on this run. Use the per-axis booleans for "how many
  wells did this screen catch".

**Deliberately not done**

* **`mean_INT` was not made a gate.** It is the statistic that would catch the
  uniformly-bright samples the burden test structurally cannot — which is exactly
  why it is tempting. But background intensity is a continuous nuisance covariate
  affecting every sample, not a population of bad wells. Gating on it would
  delete real variation. Model it instead.
* **The PCA cut was not loosened** to reach bright wells. On this run the
  brightest wells sit *below* the PCA cut on `PC_z`, so lowering it admits dim
  wells before it admits a single bright one. The instrument is not turned down;
  it is pointed elsewhere.
* **PCA round 2 was not deleted** although it fired on nothing here. It is now
  reported as INERT with its headroom, which is a statement about this run, not
  about the screen.

## G.2 Questions this pipeline cannot answer

**Clustering by clinical collection site.** Primary QC is agnostic to phenotype
and covariates by design, and the site label only exists after the metadata
merge. D.5.4 tests the *physical position on the plate*, which is a different
question that happens to share the word "site" — and which is what surfaced the
worst-position and corner-gradient findings. For collection site, join
`well_level_QC.csv` to the merged metadata; `Secondary_QC/Triage_Review/` already
does this.

**Whether the read flag is redundant given depth.** See D.5.5 — it has been shown
to be *small*, which is not the same as shown to be *nothing*.
